prepareData.title: Prepare your data
prepareData.intro: The Legonizer reads 3D Tiles, glTF/GLB, OBJ and CityJSON. Here is how to get one of them from the data you have.

citygml.title: From CityGML
citygml.body: Convert your CityGML files to CityJSON with citygml-tools, a free, maintained tool that reads CityGML 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0 (it needs Java 17 or later, or Docker). This command writes city.json next to city.gml; drop city.json on the Import step:
citygml.crop: A whole city is too big for a browser: cut out your district first, giving its corners in the coordinates of your file, then convert city__subset.gml:
citygml.note: py3dtilers, which this page suggested before, was discontinued in January 2025, and py3dtiles, which its authors point to, does not read CityGML.

osm.title: From OpenStreetMap buildings
osm.body: Export the buildings of your area as a 3D model (glTF or OBJ), for example with a Blender add-on that imports OpenStreetMap data. Check the size summary after import.

blender.title: From Blender
blender.body: Export as glTF 2.0 (.glb). Apply the object transforms first. If the model looks too small or too big after import, change the unit on the Import step.

qgis.title: From QGIS
qgis.body: Export your 3D scene to OBJ (3D map view, Export menu, Export 3D Scene). Keep the model in a projected coordinate system in metres.

size.title: Keep it light
size.body: Files up to about 2 million triangles (300 MB) work on a typical laptop. Crop to your district before exporting, or simplify the model.

units.title: Check units and orientation
units.body: After import, the summary shows the model's size in metres. A city 0.4 m wide means the unit is wrong: pick the right one in the summary. If buildings lie on their side, change the up axis.
